steps.title: Make a receipt from a list
steps.explanation: A total adds the numbers in a list. Start at zero and add one number at a time; an empty list stays at zero. let gives a value a name that you can update, and += adds to that value.
steps.task: Add x to n inside the loop to return the total.
hints: The loop visits each number once.
Inside the loop, write n += x; (this means add x to n).

steps.title: Rebuild the working instructions
steps.explanation: Keep the supplied function and result list. Rebuild the part that fills the list using the example as a guide. Re-run whenever you want to check a change.
steps.task: Fill the result list using this topic's rule.
hints: This graph has two-way links between points. A group, also called a connected component, contains all points that can reach one another. Start at point 0, then check the other points in number order. Whenever a point has not been visited, explore its whole group depth first: follow a path as far as you can before going back. Record how many points are in that group. The result list follows the order in which you first find the groups. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.
Revisit the example and copy one instruction at a time, checking what it does.
